title: Placki ziemniaczane
subtitle: Polish potato pancakes
excerpt: Grated potato pancakes fried in fat until crisp at the edges and tender within. The Polish staple eaten with soured cream and chives, or with goulash spooned over. Quick and filling weeknight cooking.
sourceNotes: Traditional Polish recipe appearing in all standard Polish home-cookery references. Equivalent to similar preparations across Central and Eastern Europe: Swiss Rösti, German Kartoffelpuffer, Jewish latkes.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch; reheat in a 200°C oven for 8 minutes to restore the crispness.

content.text: Placki ziemniaczane are Polish potato pancakes: grated raw potato mixed with egg and a little flour, fried in fat until the edges are golden and lacy. The texture is crisp outside and soft within. They are eaten with soured cream and sometimes with goulash or mushroom sauce.

Grate the peeled potatoes and onion on the coarse side of a box grater directly into a clean tea towel. Gather the towel and squeeze out as much water as possible over the sink. The drier the potato, the crisper the pancake.
Transfer to a bowl. Add the eggs, flour, salt, and pepper. Mix well.

Heat a generous layer of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. When the oil shimmers, drop spoonfuls of the potato mixture in and press flat with a spatula. Each pancake should be about 8 cm across and 1 cm thick.

Fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the edges are golden and the pancake releases cleanly from the pan. Flip and fry for 3 more minutes. Remove to kitchen paper to drain. Repeat with the remaining mixture, adding oil as needed.

items.symptom: The pancakes break apart when flipped
items.cause: Too much moisture in the potato or not enough flour
items.fix: Squeeze the potato more thoroughly. Add an extra tablespoon of flour.

items.symptom: The pancakes are pale and greasy
items.cause: Oil not hot enough when pancakes were added
items.fix: Test the oil with a small drop of batter; it should sizzle immediately. Fry in batches to avoid cooling the oil.

items.symptom: The pancakes taste raw in the centre
items.cause: Made too thick or the heat was too high, charring the outside before the inside cooked
items.fix: Keep pancakes to 1 cm thick. Reduce heat slightly if the edges brown too quickly.

items.cause: Oxidation while the potato sat after grating
items.fix: Fry immediately after grating, or keep the grated potato in cold water and squeeze dry just before cooking.

content.text: Potato pancakes exist across Central and Eastern Europe under different names but with a broadly shared method. In Poland they appear as a fast supper dish or a side, always with soured cream, sometimes alongside barszcz (beetroot soup). In autumn and winter they are made from fresh potatoes; in the rest of the year they are equally good. Serve the pancakes immediately while still crisp; they soften quickly as they cool.
